column18:
Slam Dunk: Yonkyou Gekitotsu!! (From TV Animation スラムダンク 四強激突!!) - English Translation BETA v0.1

Bandai's 1994 Super Famicom basketball game, based on the Slam Dunk anime and released only in Japan. Story mode follows Shohoku through the Kanagawa prefectural tournament. Hanamichi Sakuragi, Rukawa, Akagi, Mitsui and Miyagi train, argue and fight their way through Shoyo, Kainan and Ryonan, with one goal: a ticket to the Inter-High. Between matches the anime's story plays out in narrated scenes and dialogue, and Coach Anzai puts the team through training mini-games. Your scores there affect the players on the court. There's also an Exhibition mode to play any match you want.

The game has five endings. Lose to Shoyo, or come up short against Ryonan, and the tournament ends right there. Win it all and Shohoku goes to the Inter-High. There's also a hidden special ending: ace the training before the fifth match and beat Ryonan in the last one by 20 points or more, without losing to Shoyo or Kainan along the way.
The passwords speak Slam Dunk

This is what we're proudest of. The cartridge has no battery, so story progress is saved with passwords. In the original those were Japanese phrases typed on a kana keyboard, and almost every one is a line, a nickname or an in-joke from the series. We didn't turn them into random codes. The keyboard is now Latin, and each of the 53 passwords became an English phrase that keeps the joke:
- ゴリラじじい → OLDGORILLA
- あかげザル → REDMONKEY
- メガネくん → FOUREYES
- ドンマイみつい → CHINUPMITSUI
- ナンバーワンルーキー → NO.1ROOKIE
- ぎゃふんといわしてやる → EATYOURWORDS

Each password still takes you back to exactly the same point in the story as the Japanese one it replaces.
What's in the patch
- All 601 messages translated: story scenes, narration, chapter titles, training instructions and results, referee calls, match panels, statistics and the ending credits.
- Graphics redrawn in English: the title screen subtitle (Clash of the Four Powers), the scoreboard, the command and pass panels, the lineup and tactics screens, the league table and the password keyboard.
- A new half-width font. The original box fits 12 Japanese characters per line, so few that the Japanese itself splits words in half. The new font fits 24 letters, so every sentence is written out in full instead of being chopped up.
- ROM expanded to 2 MB to make room for the English script, with all 831 text pointers relocated and checked.
- Two bugs from the original cartridge fixed:
- The anti-piracy check is disarmed. It fires on PAL consoles and on setups that write to cartridge memory, leaving a black screen and garbled text.
- A memory corruption crash is fixed. It came from an interrupt running with the wrong register size, and it could turn the whole screen into garbage.
- Every message was shown on screen and checked so nothing runs off the box. Every text was reviewed twice against the Japanese: once for meaning, and once by a reader who only sees the English, the way a player reads it.
Why it's a beta

Nobody has played the game through from the first match to an ending yet. We put every message on screen, read over 2,130 screenshots of the translated game, and reached all five endings to check their text. But to get there, the match results were forced through memory, so the matches themselves weren't played. The text should all be there and fit its boxes. What a beta can still hide is a problem that only shows up in a real playthrough. The full release comes once the game has been played to every ending.

- Japanese passwords from the original won't work on the patched ROM. If you had one written down, its English equivalent takes you to the same place.

Ninja Burai Densetsu (忍者武雷伝説) - English Translation BETA v0.1

Sega's 1991 Mega Drive tactical RPG, released only in Japan. It's a grid strategy game with seven unit classes, units that die for good, and a deadline in days for every chapter. Your soldiers' health shows up as lit candles instead of numbers.

The story is one the cartridge assumes you already know. A European ship runs aground on the coast of Japan, and a three-year-old boy survives the wreck. A ninja takes him in and raises him under the name Burai. Years later, Nobunaga has fallen under the power of the sword Kusanagi and become a demon, and Burai sets out with his companions to stop him. The campaign runs through ten chapters, nine of them named after real historical districts of the Tōhoku region in northern Japan.
The script was never stored as text

This is what we're proudest of. There's no Japanese text in this ROM to translate, at least not in any form a text tool can find. Every dialogue screen is stored as compressed graphics: a block with the unique 8×8 tiles of the finished screen, and a tilemap that puts them back in order. The characters live in the pictures, and the order lives in the map.

To translate it, we reimplemented both of the game's compression formats from the disassembly (a Huffman scheme for graphics and an LZ variant for tilemaps). Then we read the whole script out of the tile data, translated it, and replaced the picture-based dialogue with real text in a new Latin font. The original box fits 15 Japanese characters per line. The new one fits 31.
What's in the patch
- The full script in English: all 110 dialogue boxes and the 10 scenes of the opening narration, from villagers and shopkeepers to temples, castles and the defeat screen.
- The whole interface: battle commands, the sidebar, status and combat screens, all 41 item names, options, shops, the inn, and the village, temple and castle panels.
- Graphics redrawn in English: the title logo (Legend of the Ninja Burai), the chapter title cards, the Record Book save and load screens, the defeat screen and the EXIT signs.
- A new Latin font with lowercase. The original only had capital A-Z, used for a few labels.
- ROM expanded from 1 MB to 2 MB to make room for the English script and graphics.
- Names and terms follow the official 1991 strategy guide. Masamune and Muramasa are the legendary swordsmiths, Tanegashima is the island where the arquebus first reached Japan, and Kusanagi is one of the three imperial regalia. Martial ranks stay as dan (1 DAN), the way the game counts them, not "Level 1".
- Every text was reviewed twice against the Japanese: once for meaning, and once by a reader who only sees the English, the way a player reads it. Every box was measured so nothing runs past its edges, and the save and continue cycle was tested end to end.
Why it's a beta

Nobody has played the game through to the final chapter yet. We put every one of the 120 dialogue screens on screen in the translated ROM and read them there, and we reached the defeat ending in a real run. To see the late-game text, we used a debug build and forced our way through, so the later chapters weren't actually played. The text should all be there and fit its boxes. What a beta can still hide is a problem that only shows up in a real playthrough. The full release comes once the game has been played to the end.
Good to know
- Two things stay in Japanese on purpose: the brush-painted logo on the boot screen and the 林火山 scroll on the dojo wall. Both are artwork, and we kept them as they are.
- The game opens with a short Patch Clan screen (BETA V0.1 BUILD 15).

Description
A clean 2-byte instruction patch for QuackShot that forces English text on all regions while keeping native PAL/NTSC video timing intact. Corrects the internal header checksum.By default, running the World ROM on Japanese hardware or region settings forces Japanese text along with 60 Hz timing. Standard region-unlock hacks often overwrite the register checks completely, which can break proper 50 Hz/60 Hz detection on PAL hardware.

This patch cleanly separates video timing from language selection:
- Language Lock: Forces the game engine to load the non-Japanese text script regardless of hardware region.
- Preserved Video Timing: Modifies the M68K initialization routine to set the Overseas flag in RAM while preserving register D0. The console retains its native refresh rate (60 Hz on NTSC/JP, 50 Hz on PAL).
- Checksum Fix: Updates the internal Mega Drive header checksum to eliminate warning screens on real flashcarts and emulators.

Dragon Ball 3: Gokuu Den (Famicom) — Complete English Translation v1.1

Bandai's Dragon Ball 3: Gokuu Den (ドラゴンボール3 悟空伝, TOSE, 1989) came out only in Japan. It tells Goku's story from the first Dragon Ball hunt to the World Tournament, and it plays like a board game: you move across the map, draw cards and fight with them.

This patch is the first complete English translation. You can now play the whole game in English from start to finish. Version 1.1 adds battery saves and a fast-text option, makes battles quicker, and fixes six bugs that have been on the cartridge since 1989.

> An earlier partial patch by Dodgy Translations (v0.15, 2000) covered the menus and the intro. This one covers the entire game.
Links
- 📥 Patch: https://www.patchclan.com/#/jogo/dragon-ball-3
(direct IPS: https://www.patchclan.com/patches/dragon-ball-3-en.ips)
- 📖 Manual (English, updated for v1.1): https://www.patchclan.com/#/manual/dragon-ball-3
- ▶️ Full longplays on YouTube (v1.1, no commentary):
- Ending A: https://youtu.be/s1WjVy2gNNY
- Ending B + secret fights: https://youtu.be/xInWQR3Hrz4
- Playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQ0gqG-q15Wo

Also available in Portuguese and Spanish on the same page.
Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| | |
| | |
| | |
| | |
| | |

---
What's in the patch
🗨️ Translation
- 1,305 of 1,305 script messages in English, plus all 40 battle and training messages
- 66 characters and enemies, 14 special moves and 16 battle names, using Viz's official names (Kami's Lookout, General Blue, Mercenary Tao, Ma Junior, Basho Fan…)
- Every line fits the game's 3-line × 24-column box, and the engine has no way to continue a message onto a second box. 164 messages ran to 45+ glyphs in Japanese and were rewritten to fit without losing their meaning
- Checked against Bandai's 1989 instruction manual. That is how we caught that the 体 card means body slam, which is an attack, and not defense
🎨 Graphics that were text
- Card symbols: the ten kanji (拳 蹴 連 必 術 逃 ? 体 特 武) are drawn tiles, so they were redrawn as three-letter labels in a 5×7 mini font: PCH KCK CMB FIN MAG RUN ? BDY SPC WPN
- Defense balls: the kanji numerals 一–六 now read 1–6
- Title logo: 悟空伝 redrawn as LEGEND OF GOKU in the same 96×32 px
- Password screen: Latin letters, no look-alike symbols, and every original password still works
- ROM program space expanded from 128 KB to 256 KB to fit the English text
⭐ New in v1.1: quality of life
- Battery save: 2 slots, each with a backup copy. Save from the SELECT menu, and CONTINUE on the title screen lists both slots. Passwords still work
- Text speed screen at power-on, with its own artwork: on Fast, text runs 2× faster and card animations speed up too
- Hold the D-pad and Goku keeps walking until the path turns, so you no longer tap once per square
- The card cursor on the map wraps around from the 5th card to the 1st
- Faster battles: the enemy's card stays up for half a second, the pause after each attack is shorter, and duel cards confirm by themselves (no more double confirmation). You get half a second to take back the last card with B
🖥️ New in v1.1: screen fixes
- Each card's stars now show as a number
- The last Japanese text on the board, the 魔 ("demon") space, is now a demon's head icon
- Flicker removed: lines flickered under the enemy's cards and in the text box, in battles and on adventure screens. The original cartridge does this too, because it switches graphics banks in the middle of a scanline. The screen-split routines were rewritten to switch during horizontal blank
- The pink-and-white striped frame that showed along the edge of the world map while scrolling (also in the original) is gone
🐞 Original cartridge bugs fixed (v1.1)

| # | Bug in the 1989 cartridge | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fake Goku softlock (Demon Castle): beat the Fake Goku, leave the room and come back. The screen garbles and the game freezes with a constant buzz | An event-script jump landed in the middle of an instruction and the CPU hit an illegal opcode. 1 byte |
| 2 | Running from Fake Goku with the RUN card caused the same freeze | Same cause, same fix |
| 3 | Level 31 bug: reaching level 30 by winning a fight jumped straight to level 31 with max HP and max special points set to 0 | The level-31 entries in two tables were empty. Filled in (threshold 522,000, max 228/228, between Lv30 and Lv32). 5 bytes |
| 4 | Training points reset: a level-up from training on Kami's Lookout could drop your total training points back to 7,380 | A level-up can no longer lower your total |
| 5 | Glitch passwords: six known forged passwords put Goku in impossible states (black screen, off the board, invisible, stuck) | Those six are now rejected. All legitimate passwords work as before |
| 6 | General Blue + Mouse: using the Mouse item skipped the stat recalculation, so on turn 1 General Blue fought with Buyon's stats from the previous battle | Recalculation now runs. 4 bytes |

Each bug was first reproduced on the Japanese ROM, then shown to be gone on the patched ROM. The bug reports come from the Japanese fan sites gcgx.games and ゲームの里 (gesato).

Left as in the original, on purpose: the partial-cartridge-insertion glitch (a hardware trick used by speedrunners), the extra Senzu Beans at Korin Tower before drinking the Sacred Water (a script loophole), and the unused special moves that only passwords can unlock.
✏️ Fixes to our own v1.0
- Battle name bar: some names came out cut or wrong (Jackie Chun showed as illin). The bar now has its own name table
- About 150 text and label edits (script lines, Adventure menu, status screens, move and enemy names), e.g. Jan-Ken, Afterimage, N'cha Cannon, Basho Fan, plus clearer training instructions: "Play a card with equal or more defense!"

---
How to patch
- Base ROM: Dragon Ball 3 - Gokuu Den (Japan) (Rev 1).nes
MD5 0bc3d5d7d1e7f2206ce1c157402ff944
- Patch: dragon-ball-3-en.ips. Apply it with Flips, Lunar IPS or the web patcher at https://www.patchclan.com/aplicador/
- Saving uses Bandai's EEPROM (mapper 16, submapper 5). It was tested in Mesen and FCEUmm but not yet on real hardware or flash carts. If your emulator doesn't save, passwords still work.

The release build was played from power-on to both endings, and the longplays above are those runs.
Credits

Patch Clan · www.patchclan.com · project lead: Sonix

Fan translation. Patch only; we never distribute ROMs.

English Translation v1.0

I've completed an English fan translation of the 1999 PlayStation game Macross: Do You Remember Love?, covering both discs.

To my knowledge, this is the first publicly available complete English text translation of the PlayStation version.
What's Translated
- All in-game dialogue across both discs, including stage-specific conversations and gameplay instructions.
- Menus, options and controller configuration.
- Weapon descriptions, system messages and disc-changing prompts.

The original Japanese voices, music, cinematics and artwork have been preserved. FMVs remain in Japanese and have not been subtitled. The subtitle of "Do you remember love?" was left in Japanese as it is left as such in the movie's marketing and even the recent announcement regarding the movie in the west.
Known Limitations

Disc 1 contains a small number of minor dialogue-rendering glitches. Certain letters may briefly flicker, disappear or display incorrect graphical tiles.

These issues stem from adapting the original Japanese game's text-rendering system to accommodate longer English dialogue. After extensive debugging and testing, I chose to prioritise stability and preserve the original game's appearance rather than introduce further risks attempting to eliminate every graphical imperfection.

The more significant dialogue-rendering issues encountered during development of Disc 2 were successfully resolved.

These remaining imperfections do not prevent the game from being completed or enjoyed in English.
Testing and Compatibility

Both discs have been completed from beginning to end on original PlayStation hardware.

The final xdelta patches have also been independently tested and verified to reproduce the intended English game images correctly.
Installation

1. Obtain your own Japanese BIN/CUE images of both discs.
2. Use a standard xdelta patching utility, such as Delta Patcher.
3. Apply each .xdelta patch to its corresponding original Japanese BIN file.
4. Use the supplied English CUE files to launch the patched game in DuckStation or a compatible PlayStation hardware setup.

The included README provides the supported original BIN checksums and basic instructions. Other disc image versions are not guaranteed to be compatible.
Final Notes

This project was completed through reverse engineering of the original PlayStation game's executables, dialogue system and proprietary resource formats, without access to the original source code.

The aim was to produce a faithful English localisation while preserving the original gameplay, presentation, music and overall experience.

This is an unofficial, non-commercial fan translation. No complete game images or copyrighted game assets are distributed.

Enjoy!

Famicom Jump: Heroes History (ファミコンジャンプ 英雄列伝) - Definitive Edition v2.1

Famicom Jump: Eiyuu Retsuden came out on February 25, 1989, from Bandai with TOSE, to mark the 20th anniversary of Weekly Shōnen Jump. A boy reading the magazine gets pulled inside it and has to save Jump World from King Piccolo, recruiting heroes from Dragon Ball, Fist of the North Star, JoJo, Saint Seiya, Kinnikuman, City Hunter and more. It's an action RPG with boss fights played like a fighting game, shooting, sports and racing minigames and, at the end, a command battle between 16 heroes and 13 villains.

Exploring the world map.

The boxing minigame.

Translation: BlackPaladin & Patch Clan. This edition keeps BlackPaladin's English translation (v1.03), reviewed line by line against the Japanese and made in partnership with him: the opening screen carries the credit. It adds saving, a talk button, pause in fights, a wider text box and a set of fixes. Since his translation was v1.03, the Definitive Edition starts at v2.0.

FULL LONGPLAY

English script

• Four missing lines are back. They came out blank or with a piece of another line, though every one has text in the Japanese. The most visible: when Shenron appears, the wish box used to be empty and now reads "Revive our friends!". The other three are the line about the cloud ("Master Roshi's Flying Nimbus would let me fly‥"), a refusal in a fight ("I-I can't raise a hand to my teacher!") and "Out of energy‥ no strength left‥".

Left, v1.03: Shenron appears and the box is empty. Right, the same scene with "Revive our friends!".

• Restaurant. Three lines that came out as garbled letters, like "EGvHKt JeneMX!", are now in English: "Oh dear, sir‥ You can't eat! Not enough!"

• The whole script reread against the Japanese. 78 lines changed to sit closer to the original meaning. The baseball line, for one, is now "Isn't baseball something you eat?". In one of them, "Kaioh" stood where Tonchinkan should be: the Japanese is かいとう とんちんかん, Tonchinkan the thief.

The baseball minigame.

• Official names. In a separate pass, 51 lines changed names to follow the official American ones (Viz and Funimation). Dialogue always says Master Roshi, where Muten Roshi and Turtle Hermit also showed up before, plus Flying Nimbus and 44 Magnum spelled one way. In the shop, the item is still Kinto'un.

The items menu, all in English.

• Spelling and meaning. Spelling and agreement fixes, and one spelling per name: Nyorai, Musou, Vacuum, Keppaden. Where the line means Jotaro, it now says "…see Jotaro again.", and a line that had slipped into the past is back in the future, as in the Japanese ("now revive").

• On-screen details. No more periods alone on a line, sentences starting in lower case, lines opening with a space or run-together words. A fight line that spilled outside its box now stays inside it.

• Lines that fit the box (new in v2.1). 24 lines that sat badly in the wider box, with one word alone on a line or a sentence split in the middle, were rewritten. "Thank you for supporting / Famicom Jump." now reads "Thanks for supporting Famicom Jump.", and minigame instructions read "Press B to fire".

New in v2.1: the same line in v2.0 (left) and v2.1 (right).

• End credits. 12 spellings in the Japanese staff list now follow the original cartridge's romaji, and "Satoshi Kodama" became Satoshi Shimomura.

Screens

• Edition screen. Before the title comes a screen with Shenron around the border, drawn from the game's own art, plus the edition name, the version, the translation credit and the site. It stays 5 seconds, and A or START skips it. The original title screen follows, untouched.

The edition screen: version 2.1 and the translation credit.

• Shop. Two-line item names used to sit on top of the icon. Now the name goes beside the picture and the price above it.

The price above each item and the name beside the picture.

• Password grid. Four cells showed scraps of letters where the Japanese had syllables. They are now ♥ ★ ● ▲, and existing passwords still work.

Text engine

• A 22-letter box. The upper text box went from 17 to 22 letters per line and wraps by word, so the word-joining trick from v1.03 is no longer needed. The lower box stays at 17.

• Compressed text. The script is now stored as letter pairs (DTE), and the block that holds it went from 15,191 to 10,079 bytes, about a third smaller. On screen it looks the same.

Gameplay and saving

• Talk button. Your ally only spoke after 1.1 to 1.6 seconds of the hero standing still in front of him, and he looks just like an enemy: pressing A on reflex hit him and knocked down the hero's Soul. Now pressing A while your ally is waiting makes him talk right away. Enemies still take the hit, and anyone who'd rather wait still can.

• Saving. The original only kept your progress as a 40-character password. Now, when the monolith shows the password, the game saves. At power-on, CONTINUE opens with the password already filled in and the cursor on Enter, so you just press A. The password still works. After a game over, the title comes back with the cursor already on CONTINUE.

CONTINUE after a save: all 40 characters already filled in. On the grid, the new ♥ ★ ● ▲.

• Pause in fights. The original had none. START freezes the clock, the enemies and everything else; press START again to resume.

• Shot recharge. With a low Soul, the wait between shots reached 4.2 seconds; now it's 3.2. The rest of the curve is unchanged.

• Buying twice. The cartridge let you buy an item you already owned, took the money and gave you nothing. Now the shop warns you ("Cola is already yours!"): A still buys, B backs out.

The shop warns you before charging twice.

• Final battle. On the path of duels, Run wiped your wins without warning. Now the first Run warns you ("Run again: wins are lost"), and only the second one leaves. The game also remembers the last hero you picked and drops a repeated confirmation.

The first Run on the path to the castle now comes with a warning.

• Faster text. In map dialogue, holding A prints two letters per frame, and the opening plays in about half the time. Never in fights or minigames.

• Skippable trips. Mr. Time's time-travel animation runs 526 frames, close to 9 seconds, and comes back all game long. Now A or START skips it, and you land in the same era and place. The other travel animation, the Express Delivery, skips too.

Cartridge

• Same chip, more graphics. It's still Bandai's mapper 16, and the program stays at 256 KB, the most that mapper can address. Only graphics memory doubled, from 128 to 256 KB, for the edition screen's art: the file goes from 393,232 to 524,304 bytes. The NES 2.0 header now declares the chip with save memory (submapper 5, battery, 256 bytes).

Good to know

• Apply the patch to the clean Japanese ROM, not to BlackPaladin's already translated v1.03.

• Saving needs an emulator that supports Bandai's mapper 16 EEPROM boards. We tested it in Mesen. The password still works everywhere.

Credits

• Original English translation (v1.03): BlackPaladin, with Zynk Oxhyde (logo), phonymike and Gideon Zhi (programming), cccmar (testing), Cavery210 (bug reports) and scum (Mesen fix).

• Definitive Edition: Patch Clan, in partnership with BlackPaladin.

ROM

Famicom Jump - Eiyuu Retsuden (Japan), iNES with header:

• Size: 393,232 bytes

• CRC32: 80B4C1DE

• MD5: 8d8f6600197f0f4e9f92c5ef72ec9b9d

• SHA-1: fc99b28e592abd17af7d9f4cc0a5f0f12442888b

• Without the 16-byte header: 393,216 bytes, CRC32 D343C66A, MD5 9b84ccc692c97134f4936ca50e660741. Use the headered ROM.

• Patch: Famicom Jump - Eiyuu Retsuden (Japan) - Definitive Edition v2.1 build 4 (EN).ips

• Patched ROM: 524,304 bytes, CRC32 05FB52BD, MD5 23c46eb6f12a12a52024cdfab242ab4b

Patch only. We never distribute ROMs.

Jump in

Grab the patch, round up the heroes and tell us how it goes. If anything breaks or reads wrong, post it here with a screenshot and where you were in the game.

Our other translations and how to support the work: www.patchclan.com

column18:
Ultraman Club 2: Kaettekita Ultraman Club (帰ってきたウルトラマン倶楽部) - English Translation v1.0

Ultraman Club 2: Kaettekita Ultraman Club came out in Japan only, on April 7, 1990, from Yutaka with Bandai, developed by Interlink. It was also the debut of Kenji Eno, later the creator of D, credited as planner. It's a Famicom RPG where the Ultras are big-headed figures: you play MAN, the hero, and travel from Earth to the Moon, Planet Dokkun, the Monster Graveyard and Planet Ultra with Seven, Jack, Ace and Taro, against the kaiju and aliens of the series, from Baltan and Metron to Zetton and King Joe. Your allies carry capsule monsters that can fight in their place.

The title screen, redrawn in English.

Story dialogue in the 22-column box.

Translation, fixes and improvements: Patch Clan. This is the first complete English translation, revised and read on screen, and the game was played from start to finish on this build. It also fixes the cartridge's own mistakes in names and graphics, and adds an OPTIONS menu with ten settings on the title screen.

FULL LONGPLAY

Watch the full longplay on YouTube:

https://youtu.be/b7VZOibUjkE

English script

• 653 text entries. 447 messages (dialogue, battle, item descriptions, the ending and the credits), 56 entries for menus, moves and items, and 146 battle entries that hold the whole bestiary.

• Names from the series. Every kaiju and alien name was checked against the Japanese manual and the names the series uses. Plazma and Minazma follow Tsuburaya's spelling.

Zetton's challenge.

• Punctuation in the font. The game's font had no period, comma, apostrophe or hyphen. All four were drawn over kanji the English text no longer uses.

• A bigger cartridge. English did not fit in the original 128 KB of program, so it grew to 256 KB. Graphics memory doubled too, for the edition screen.

Screens

• Edition screen. Before the title comes a screen with Ultraman flying over the Earth, plus the edition name, the version and the site. The title screen follows, with the logo redrawn in English and the new OPTIONS item.

The edition screen: version 1.0.

Mistakes from the original cartridge, fixed

• Seagorath and Seamons. They had each other's names, and the Japanese manual has the same mix-up. They are now the right way around.

• Eight misspelled monsters. The Japanese misspells eight monster names. The English uses the right ones: Gavadon, Gamakujira, Crazygon, Pandon, Sartan, Alien Valdac, Alien Hipporit and Alien Flip.

Gavadon, spelled the way the series spells it. The cartridge says "Gabadon".

• The Specium Ray shout. The cartridge shouts "Juwa!". Ultraman says "Shuwatch!", and so does the English.

• Alien Babarue and Alien Magma. The two had each other's sprites. Each one now shows up with its own.

Alien Babarue before (left) and in v1.0 (right).

• Tyrant's arms. They were drawn on the wrong sides. They are now redrawn the right way.

A boss who has heard about Babarue.

Graphics

• Bosses on the map. Six bosses used to stand on the map as a generic monster figure. Now Mefilas, Kodaigon, Bemstar, Tyrant, Yapool and the Gylas brothers each have their own map sprite.

Kodaigon on the map, before (left) and in v1.0 (right).

• Series colors. Eight monsters now use colors closer to the TV series: Woo, Telesdon, Antlar, King Joe, Eleking, Zetton, Metron and Pandon.

Zetton before (left) and in v1.0 (right).

OPTIONS menu

A new OPTIONS item on the title screen opens ten settings. Every one of them can be switched back to play the way the cartridge plays, and your choices are kept in the save memory.

The ten options, with their default values.

• AUTO SAVE (on). The original only gives you a password, the 12-character Ultra Sign, at each Ultra base. Now the game also saves at that moment, and CONTINUE on the title takes you straight back there. With it off, CONTINUE asks for the password as before.

• QUICK TEXT (on). Battle messages go by faster.

• ALWAYS RUN (on). The party runs on the map without holding B.

• ENCOUNTERS (half). Random battles come half as often. NORMAL brings back the original rate.

• WEAK FOES (normal). Battles against groups far below your level: NORMAL keeps them all, HALF cuts them in half, NONE removes them.

• KEEP EXP (on). After a game over, the original takes your EXP back to what it was at your last password. Now you keep it.

• DOUBLE EXP (on). Battles give twice the EXP until Ace joins the party, to cut the early grinding.

• RUIN RAY GUARD (on). Some monsters' Ruin Ray knocks a fighter out in one hit. It can no longer knock out MAN.

• ALLY TAKEOVER (on). In the original, the battle ends in game over the moment MAN falls, even with allies still standing. Now the fight goes on while an ally is up.

• HIDE USELESS KO (on). Instant-kill moves are left out of the move list against bosses that are immune to them.

Always on

• Capsule help. The capsule list on the map shows what the highlighted capsule does: REVIVES FALLEN ALLIES, WARPS BACK TO BASE, ESCAPES A DUNGEON, FULLY HEALS THE PARTY and so on.

• Woo capsule. In the original, using Woo with nobody knocked out wasted the capsule. Now it stays in your stock.

Since v0.9

Our earlier patch (v0.9, build 36) had problems of its own, all fixed in 1.0:

• Many messages with a page break opened the wrong text after the pause.

• Lines that filled all 22 columns left an empty line after them.

• Party panel names, status labels and one 12-letter item name are fixed.

Good to know

• Apply the patch to the clean Japanese ROM, not to an earlier English patch.

• Saving uses battery-backed memory, declared in the NES 2.0 header. We tested it in Mesen. The password still works everywhere.

• The Ultra Sign password is still made of kana, as in the original: those symbols are the code you write down, so they stay.

• Two things are left for v1.1. With ALWAYS RUN on, the party also runs inside towns and castles, and in the Moon castle one floor tile under the party can flicker. In the capsule list on the map, the help line sits right under the Ultra's name, so it can read as one sentence ("JACK / FIGHTS IN YOUR PLACE").

ROM

Ultraman Club 2 - Kaettekita Ultraman Club (Japan), iNES with header:

• Size: 262,160 bytes

• CRC32: C23926CD

• MD5: 1e479bfe8e4d3c36de37dfb96aa8e68c

• SHA-1: b031678ec59993e12f84e42e9244e8ab5ce26b4d

• Without the 16-byte header: 262,144 bytes, CRC32 7980C4F7, MD5 4720fa58e54c1bdb87ac58b2e2c3584a. Use the headered ROM.

• Patched ROM: 524,304 bytes, CRC32 78BF2BF9, MD5 e2a2b3a58411ed28cd7f640cf13ed1b8

Patch only. We never distribute ROMs.

Grab the patch, pick your options and tell us how it goes. If anything breaks or reads wrong, post it here with a screenshot and where you were in the game.

=== DESCRIPTION ===

Captain Tsubasa IV: Pro no Rival-tachi - PLUS
Version 1.3

A complete Spanish AND English translation of Tecmo's Super Famicom RPG-soccer game,
built on top of a byte-exact disassembly of the game. Both languages live in the same
ROM and are switched from a new OPTIONS screen on the title menu. No gameplay value,
formula or table has been altered.

--- CHANGELOG ---

Version 1.3
One more fix, from a player report. Saves made with 1.0 or 1.2 load unchanged.
Fixes:
- Commentator lines that the match removes on its own (results, special techniques) and
that take two pages, such as "...and advance to the final!!" at the end of
Brazil - Colombia, could show their second page without the speech bubble if the
button was pressed late. Those pages now turn by themselves (or with the button), within
the time the original game leaves the line on screen.

Version 1.2
A bug-fix update, from player reports and a review of the routes and windows that 1.0
had barely exercised. Nothing about the simulation changed. Saves made with 1.0 load
unchanged.
Fixes:
- On a real cartridge with fresh battery memory, the title screen could come up in
English while OPTIONS showed Spanish. The language setting is now checked at power-on.
- The lowercase "w" of the Spanish and English font was hard to read; it was redrawn.
- Broken scene text: when a message with instant text continued on a new page, the last
line stayed hidden until the button was pressed, then appeared on the first row, and
the next page was written over it. The scene against Milcevic in the Brazil - Colombia
match was the one reported ("pierna...rle en la"); every message of that kind is fixed.
- Long technique and team names no longer run out of the commentator's speech bubble.
The text now wraps at a word and, if the rows run out, continues on a new page.
- Compact labels still in Japanese in the order windows are now translated, in both
languages.
- Cut-off options in the direction cross of the action windows ("Pa + Shot" is now
"Pass + Shot"): the game was still centring them by their Japanese length.
- Text stuck together or over the window frame in several windows: the help windows shown
with R, the file menu, the captain and penalty kicker menus, and others.
- Two of the coach's tips at the team meeting started halfway across the window, and two
lines of dialogue left a stray full stop after the player's name (Spanish).
- The route question after the deciding matches now says Si / No in Spanish instead of
YES / NO, and it calls the Brazilian preseason by the same name as the tournament title.
Note:
- The route question itself works as in the original game: on a first run, the result of
the match decides the route, and the question appears once a route has been finished
with that save file.

Version 1.0
First release.

--- LANGUAGES ---
- Spanish and English, selectable at any time from the title screen (OPTIONS ->
Idioma / Language). Spanish is the default. The setting is stored in a free area of
the cartridge's battery-backed RAM, so it survives power cycles, and it never touches
the save slots.
- The translation covers the whole game: the story scenes, the in-match commentator and
the players' lines, every menu, the match HUD, team / player / technique / action
names, the pre-match meeting and the coach's advice, the screen that presents each
match (tournament, stage, match number and teams), the name entry screen, the
ALL STAR mode, the ending and the staff credits.
- The English script was translated from the Spanish one, so both languages tell
exactly the same story.
- Player names keep their original Japanese romanisation in both languages (Tsubasa,
Hyuga, Misaki...). Foreign players use the spelling of their own country.
- Spanish text uses neutral Spanish.
- No line was shortened to make it fit: when a translated message is longer than its
box, it continues on a new page.
- The title screen subtitle (the "Pro no Rival-tachi" kana) is redrawn as RIVALES PRO
in Spanish and PRO RIVALS in English, with Latin letters in the same style as the
original (pink fill, dark outline), and it changes as soon as the language is
switched.
- Japanese is not selectable in this release.

--- TEXT AND FONTS ---
- New 8x8 Latin font with the full set of Spanish characters (accented vowels, n-tilde,
u-diaeresis, inverted question and exclamation marks), based on the scene font of
Tecmo's own Ninja Gaiden Trilogy, the same one used in the Captain Tsubasa III PLUS
translation.
- Story scenes and meeting boxes start their text next to the left border, so every
line holds more characters than the original Japanese layout allowed.
- The name entry screen has a Latin alphabet grid with the Spanish letters.
- The screen that presents each match uses new capital letters with a drop shadow,
drawn in the style of the original title font of that screen.
- The ball-holder panel of the match shows the player's name with variable-width
letters, and its compact labels (DRIB., PASS, SHOOT, TACKLE, GUTS) use a small font
of their own.

--- MENUS ---

Japanese is compact and Latin script is not: a name that took six kana takes up to
twelve letters. Instead of abbreviating everything, the menus were adapted:
- Name fields take all the free space up to the next column of the window.
Names that still do not fit scroll back and forth (marquee) with a pause at each
end, and stop scrolling when another window opens on top of them.
- The name shown over the radar uses the whole row when only one player is listed.
- The duel decision window ("Action?") shows full headers (Rival DF / Rival OF /
Rival GK, Your DF) and its columns are aligned with them.
- The menu cursor highlights were widened where the translated options are longer
than the Japanese ones.

--- NEW FEATURES ---
- OPTIONS screen: a new last entry on the title menu (CONTINUE / KICK OFF /
ALL STAR / OPTIONS), with the language setting (Espanol / English).
- Title screen touch-ups: a green PLUS badge under the right arm of the "IV" of the
Captain Tsubasa logo, with the logo's own gradient and outline, and an authorship
line under the copyright.

--- TECHNICAL NOTES ---
- The ROM is expanded from 1.5 MB to 4 MB (LoROM, ROM size byte updated in the
internal header). The extra space holds the two scripts, the two menu sets, the two
dictionaries, the presentation titles, the new font and the new code.
Battery-backed SRAM is unchanged (8 KB); the options use its last 16 bytes, outside
the save format.
- Nothing about the simulation was touched: stats, guts costs, level curves, duel
thresholds, the clock and the CPU behaviour are the original ones.
- The patch is distributed as a BPS file and expands the ROM, so apply it with a
patcher that supports growing files (Flips, beat). It carries the CRC32 of the
original ROM, so the patcher refuses to work on the wrong file. Apply it to an
unheadered ROM (1,572,864 bytes); if your dump has a 512-byte copier header, remove
it first.
- Tested on Mesen 2.

--- CREDITS ---
- Translation, hacking and new art: V. Hernandez, 2026.
- Contact: vhernandezm1107@gmail.com
- Font based on the scene font of Ninja Gaiden Trilogy (Tecmo, 1995).
- Built on an original, clean-room (and temporarily private) disassembly of the game; no third-party disassembly or documentation of the game was consulted.

Version 1.1

A complete Spanish AND English translation of Tecmo's Super Famicom RPG-soccer game,
built on top of a byte-exact (work in progress) disassembly of the game. Both
languages live in the same ROM and are switched from a new OPTIONS entry on the main
menu. No gameplay value, formula or table has been altered.

--- WHAT'S NEW IN 1.1 (CHANGES SINCE 1.0) ---

Version 1.1 is a bug-fix update. It came out of playing the game on a real console.
Nothing about the simulation changed, and saves and the language setting from 1.0 load
in 1.1 unchanged.

Fixes:
- Wrong default language on a real cartridge: with new battery-backed RAM, the
introduction and the title screen could appear in English while OPTIONS showed
Spanish, because they read the setting before the game checked it. The setting is now
checked at power-on. Emulators that start with blank save RAM did not show this.
- The menu that assigns orders to the R and Y buttons: the cursor highlight fell short
of the longer options, and several labels were abbreviated. The windows were enlarged
or moved so that labels fit in full ("Regate auto", "Ataque activo", "Super shot",
"Autodribble"...), and the highlight and the mark on the current choice now cover
them exactly, also in the Yes / No confirmation.
- The cursor highlight in the Defense list of the Tactics menu (Normal / Press / Counter)
now covers the whole option.

Changes:
- That menu is now called Ordenes in Spanish and Orders in English. It used to be called
Ajustes / Options, which suggested game settings and could be confused with the new
OPTIONS entry of the main menu. The English help texts in it now say "order" too.

--- LANGUAGES ---
- Spanish and English, selectable at any time from the main menu (press Start on the
title screen, then OPTIONS -> Espanol / English). Spanish is the default. The
setting is stored in a free area of the cartridge's battery-backed RAM, so it
survives power cycles, and it never touches the save slots.
- The translation covers the story scenes, the in-match commentator and the players'
lines, every menu, the match HUD, team / player / technique / action names, the
pre-match meeting and the manager's advice, the corner and free kick tactics screen
with its help pages, the name entry screen and the ALL STAR mode (VS Mode, League
and Edit PC).
- Player names keep their original Japanese romanisation in both languages (Tsubasa,
Hyuga, Wakabayashi, Misaki...). Foreign players use the spelling of their own
country (Muller, Hernandez, Savicevic...).
- No line was shortened to make it fit: when a translated message is longer than its
box, it continues on a new page, and names are never abbreviated.
- The title screen subtitle (the "Hasha no Shoukou" kanji) is redrawn as TITULO DE
CAMPEON in Spanish and TITLE OF CHAMPION in English, in the style of the original
copyright lettering.
- Japanese is not selectable in this release.

--- TEXT AND FONTS ---
- New 8x16 Latin font with upper and lower case letters and the full set of Spanish
characters (accented vowels, n-tilde, u-diaeresis, inverted question and exclamation
marks), drawn with a drop shadow to match the game's text.
- The story scene text box holds 28 characters per line instead of 22, and the
speech bubble of the pre-match meeting grows from 17x5 to 19x6 characters.
- The name entry screen has a single page with the whole Latin alphabet, upper and
lower case, and the Spanish letters.
- The big team names of the match presentation are drawn with new Latin letters.
- The labels of the special technique windows (L button) use a small font of their
own.

--- MENUS ---

Japanese is compact and Latin script is not: a name that took four kana takes up to
ten letters. Instead of abbreviating everything, the menus were adapted:
- Name fields take all the free space up to the next column of the window. Names
that still do not fit scroll back and forth (marquee) with a pause at each end.
- Wider, taller or re-laid-out windows where the translated text needs them: the
save menu after a match, the goodbye message, the squad lists, the League table and
schedule, the special technique headers and the Orders menu.
- The menu cursor highlights were widened where the translated options are longer
than the Japanese ones.

--- NEW FEATURES ---
- OPTIONS: a new last entry on the main menu (KICK OFF / CONTINUE / ALLSTAR /
OPTIONS), with the language setting (Espanol / English).
- Title screen touch-ups: a gold PLUS badge under the "V" of the Captain Tsubasa
logo, with the logo's own gradient and outline, and an authorship line under the
copyright.

--- KNOWN ISSUES ---
- Some texts are cut off: the translation is longer than the original and the scene
keeps the timing of the Japanese game, so it moves on before the text finishes
printing. You can see it, for example, in the introduction and in Carnevale's
special dribble. This will be addressed in a future version.

--- TECHNICAL NOTES ---
- The ROM is expanded from 2 MB to 4 MB (LoROM, ROM size byte updated in the
internal header). The extra space holds the two scripts, the two menu sets, the two
dictionaries, the new font and the new code. Battery-backed SRAM is unchanged
(8 KB); the options use its last bytes, outside the save format.
- Nothing about the simulation was touched: stats, guts costs, level curves, duel
thresholds, the clock and the CPU behaviour are the original ones.
- The patch is distributed as a BPS file and expands the ROM, so apply it with a
patcher that supports growing files (Flips, beat). It carries the CRC32 of the
original ROM, so the patcher refuses to work on the wrong file. Apply it to an
unheadered ROM (2,097,152 bytes); if your dump has a 512-byte copier header, remove
it first.
- Tested on Mesen 2.

--- CREDITS ---

- Contact: vhernandezm1107@gmail.com
- Built on an original, clean-room (and temporarily private) disassembly of the game; no third-party disassembly or documentation of the game was consulted.

Each story presents a strange situation. The player taps suspicious words in the story text, combines them into yes/no questions, and unlocks Secret Words until the true explanation can be given.
What's translated
- All 80 stories plus the finale: story text, Secret Words, every question and answer, hints, quizzes and explanations
- All story scenes and Anna's dialogue, including the tutorial
- Menus, buttons, save screens and system messages

- Tested from start to finish in melonDS. Not yet tested on real hardware or flash carts.

A couple of students, Takeru and his girlfriend Mizuki, crash-land on an uncharted island during their school graduation trip. Soon after, the group of survivors is attacked by a cult of natives. What are the islanders after? Will our heroes be able to fend them off and escape the curse of Ogaeritō island?

"Ningyo no rakuin" is a horror-themed tactical JRPG developed by Highwaystar and released in 2000 by NEC Interchannel for the Sony PlayStation. It plays like "Final Fantasy Tactics" but with a story heavily inspired by the works of H.P. Lovecraft.

All of the game's text has been fully translated into English. The patch is in Xdelta3 format, and included in the .ZIP file is the translated game manual and CD insert. The patch has been thoroughly tested on emulators, but if you happen to find some error or bug, please don't hesitate to get in touch and we'll fix it on a subsequent release as soon as possible.

The game doesn't recognise analogue controllers. If you can't get past the title screen, reconfigure your controller to digital in the emulator you're using.

- Walkthrough written by the translator: https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/ps/578165-ningyo-no-rakuin/faqs/82193/introduction
- RetroAchievements set made by playtester: https://retroachievements.org/game/18248

The full patch source code and assets is available on GitHub.

ABSOLUTELY NO AI WAS USED IN THE MAKING OF THIS PATCH

- Chapu - Programming/hacking.
- LaytonLoztew - Playtesting/QA, proofreading, RA set
- vervalkon - Graphics and video editing, release trailer.

Captain Tsubasa (キャプテン翼) - English Translation v1.2.0

Captain Tsubasa came out for the Famicom on April 28, 1988, from Tecmo, based on Yoichi Takahashi's soccer manga and its TV anime. Tsubasa Ozora leads Nankatsu through the national tournament and then plays for Japan at an international Jr. Youth tournament in France. It's soccer played through menus: every pass, dribble and shot is a choice, an animation plays out the result, and each move spends Guts, the players' stamina. There are two endings, depending on whether you find Misaki in Paris. In 1992 the game reached North America and Europe as Tecmo Cup Soccer Game, with almost the whole cast replaced.

The title screen, redrawn as CAPTAIN TSUBASA in the original style.

The opening.

Translation: Patch Clan. This patch puts the whole game in English and keeps the original Japanese cast. It also fixes three problems in the original cartridge and adds a battery save with five slots. Version 1.2.0 was played from power-on to both endings, with and without Misaki on the team, and its text was checked on screen.

FULL LONGPLAY

Above, Ending B, without Misaki. Ending A, with Misaki, comes in two parts: Part 1 and Part 2.
English script

• The whole game in English. The match commentary, the cutscenes, the classroom scenes, the search for Misaki in Paris, the coach's menu, the player cards and the ending.

The coach's meeting after a match.

• Official names. Names follow the official English spellings of the manga and anime: Ozora, Hyuga, Wakabayashi, Karl Heinz Schneider, Elle Sid Pierre. Guts keeps its name, as in the series.

• Paris. Before the Jr. Youth tournament, Tsubasa has from 9:40 to 12:00 to look for Misaki: pick where to go, ask around and look, while the clock runs. The search is optional.

Montmartre at 9:59, during the search.

Find him and he joins the team, and the ending changes.

Ending A.

Text engine

• Twice the room for text. In the Japanese script every line takes two rows on screen, and the upper row only holds the ゛ and ゜ marks. A new control code lets English use both rows: the match windows went from 14 to 28 characters per line, and the larger ones from 18 to 36.

Match commentary using both rows of the box.

• A new font. The cartridge had only sixteen Latin letters. A new 74-tile font adds the rest of the uppercase alphabet, the lowercase letters and the punctuation.

The action menu in a match, with Ozora's stats.

Screens

• Title logo. Redrawn as CAPTAIN TSUBASA in the original style and palette, and so is the small TSUBASA logo in the classroom.

• Password screen. Latin letters and digits, under "…SHOOT YOUR SCORE MEMO!…".

• Patch Clan screen. Before the title, a screen shows the patch version.

The Patch Clan screen: version 1.2.0.

Fixes to the original cartridge

• The ball. It no longer loses its right half when it moves on the pitch. The NES draws at most eight sprites per scanline, and the ball was often the one left out.

• The score. It stops at 255 goals instead of rolling over to 0.

• Passwords. Some passwords pointed past the end of the team list, so the opponent's name came out garbled, and one of them froze the game on a black screen. They now lead to a valid opponent and the game goes on.

Saving

• Battery save, five slots. The original only gave you a password to write down. Now SAVE in the coach's menu writes your progress to the cartridge, and CONTINUE on the title screen loads it.

CONTINUE opens the five slots.

• Same data as the password. The save holds the same 24 bytes the password encodes and goes through the game's own password check.

• Passwords still work. Hold B while choosing CONTINUE to open the password screen.

Cartridge

• Same chip, more program. It's still MMC1. The program ROM went from 128 KB to 256 KB to fit the English text, so the file goes from 262,160 to 393,232 bytes. The NES 2.0 header now declares 8 KB of battery-backed save memory.

Known issues

• When Ozora's dialogue box opens at half-time, its border is drawn incomplete for a single frame (1/60 of a second). A fix is planned for the next version.

• In Ending B, without Misaki, the first letters of one line in the closing scene are cut off at the left edge of the screen.

• The cursor underline in the player list flickers, as it does on the original cartridge.

• If you hold Up while an opponent dribbles, the opponent seems to walk backwards. This comes from the original game and was left as is.

Good to know

• Apply the patch to Captain Tsubasa (Japan) with its 16-byte iNES header.

• We played the game through in Mesen. Saving was tested by closing the emulator and reopening it with the save file the game had written. It hasn't been tested on real hardware or a flash cartridge.

Credits

• Translation, fixes and improvements: Patch Clan.

• Original game: Tecmo, 1988, based on Yoichi Takahashi's Captain Tsubasa.

ROM

Captain Tsubasa (Japan), iNES with header:

• Size: 262,160 bytes

• CRC32: 0F68ED1B

• MD5: eeb77e6e0e0b5695f9a35f47979c4722

• SHA-1: ba366fefe13a3746510acab2fe73d4db1fd8dce4

• Without the 16-byte header: 262,144 bytes, CRC32 F3F1269D, MD5 8005917fdb44ab15048aef36e9030719. Use the headered ROM.

• Patch: Captain Tsubasa (Japan) - English v1.2.0.ips

• Patched ROM: 393,232 bytes, CRC32 39B9FDD0, MD5 aa0bc053572db8bba3ef9b481ee2684c

Patch only. We never distribute ROMs.

Kick off

Grab the patch, line up your eleven and tell us how it goes. If anything breaks or reads wrong, post it here with a screenshot and where you were in the game.

Our other translations and how to support the work: www.patchclan.com

Complete translation of Lord Monarch for the Super Famicom, which is a port of the classic simulation game, originally released by Nihon Falcom for the PC-98.

Lord Monarch is a real-time strategy game where your units automatically build houses, clear trees and raid enemy settlements. As long as your King stays in the castle, you collect taxes, which affect your gold income. When navigating a menu or moving the cursor, the game is paused. Lower tax leads to faster expansion and higher population growth.

While the concept seems simple at first, the maps get progressively more complex. There is also Advanced-Mode which increases difficulty by making your opponents smarter.

This port notably features a map editor and support for the SNES Mouse, plus three unique map themes.

Not AI written. All text, hacking and graphics were handmade
Most of the localization was done in 2024–2025
Some liberties were taken with map names because of space constraints

Fixed a bug in the original where parts of the interface kept the wrong color after switching to advanced mode

RF = Rate of Fire = The number of projectiles fired by the weapon per burst
